feed.title: N-brace
feed.subtitle: n-brace is a standalone, offline-first app (and Obsidian plugin) for visualizing and navigating your notes as a graph mind map.

entry.title: First version of n-brace has been released

link.title: First version of n-brace has been released

entry.content:
After three major idea iterations and a long stretch of nights and weekends, the first version of n-brace is out — as a standalone, offline-first application, no longer tied to Obsidian.

n-brace lets you visualize and navigate your notes as a graph mind map, built around the Pocket Brain technique, so you can move smoothly through large knowledge networks instead of getting lost in a wall of files.

Installers for Windows, macOS and Linux are available on the releases page, and the app will auto-update itself from here on.

Mobile support isn’t ready yet, and the Obsidian plugin remains available for anyone who prefers to stay inside Obsidian — but the standalone app is now where active development is focused.

Check the roadmap for what’s coming next.
entry.summary: n-brace grows up from an Obsidian plugin into its own standalone app

entry.title: a Roadmap
entry.content:
a Roadmap

For now I’m focusing mainly on those thing:

  1. smooth user experience, make app more user friendly
    • film some video tutorials
    • add initial and ready exemplary subgraph with all features highlighted
    • add grouping/moving operations to the app
    • add shortcuts and swift moves to the app
  2. release mobile app (currently I have no funds to maintain developer mobile app accounts)
  3. add more AI (still wondering if it’s the way)
